modalities: Certification or Compliance_carbon_market or Voluntary_carbon_market or Other
explanation:
The reason why this MRV is needed. A voluntary carbon market is a carbon market in which members are not legally compelled to reduce their emissions but do so voluntarily. These markets enable carbon emitters to offset their emissions by acquiring carbon credits generated by third-party initiatives aimed at removing or decreasing GHG emissions from the environment.  Companies can engage in the voluntary carbon market on their own or as part of an industry-wide programme. Compliance carbon markets are  also known as mandatory markets. They are governed by national, regional, or provincial law and compel emission sources to meet legally mandated GHG emissions reduction targets. Because compliance  programmes offset credits are generated and traded for regulatory compliance they typically act like, and are priced 
like, other commodities. Certification is a procedure to attribute a label.

Fixed or Reference or Distribution or Relative_Change
explanation:
Please indicate the method used to compute the threshold values. 
A Fixed value is a static value based on best available research or knowledge, stratified as required. It comes from the bilbiography. A Reference value is also a static value, calculated as a percentage of what would be found in a reference situation, where soil processes are occurring in a way that is considered to be desirable such as natural areas, stratified as required. A Distribution is a changeable value, based on the regional state of the soil (i.e., threshold defined as a certain percentile of the current observed range of values), static only until distribution is re- measured, after which the threshold may change. A threshold based on relative change is a changeable value, based on the local state of the soil (i.e., target defined as an increase or decrease of a certain percent within a specified number of years for a same place), static only for stated time span, after which the soil is re-measured, and the target will change.

Please indicate the method used to verify the results. 
The Action-based scheme is a scheme where the MRV framework is validated when the MRV user implements  defined measures (e.g. agricultural practices), independently of the resulting impact (e.g. carbon storage) of those measures.
The Result-based scheme is a scheme where he MRV framework is validated when the soil parameter value is improved (e.g. increase of the Carbon stock), without taking into account the way to reach this objective. 
Hybrid involves both an Action-based scheme and a Result-based scheme.
